stages.notes: The costume as built: heavy, upright, cheerful. Walk: a slow waddle, swing leg_L/leg_R about x by up to 25 degrees with the shin following 10 to 15 more, body rolling 3 to 4 degrees about z onto the standing leg; the hips are 2 m wide so keep the stride short. Arms swing opposite the legs, 20 degrees at the shoulder. Idle: breathe by scaling body a little, turn head up to 35 degrees about y, tilt 15 about z. The eyes never blink; let eye_L and eye_R track the player (up to 30 degrees) while the head stays still. Attack: it charges, body pitched forward 15 degrees, head down 20 so the horn leads, arms back. Jumpscare: push the head at the camera, horn first. Limits: leg 35, shin 40 (bend backward only, positive x), arm 60 forward and back and 30 out to the side (the fists pass the hips), forearm 50, head 40 about y and 25 about x before the neck opens. No jaw: the smile is sewn on. Parts: sway_1: the tail: a short rope with a tuft, hangs over the rear.

Folded into a deep crouch: rear on the floor, knees up beside the ears, long arms planted between them. The rest pose is the idle. Idle: almost still, then small wrong movements: rock body 3 degrees about x, let the head drop and snap back, twitch one forearm. The eyes do not agree (the pupils are baked off-axis), so turning eye_L and eye_R to the player still leaves them looking two ways. Walk: it does not stand. Move it as a crawl or a frog hop: both arms reach forward (arm about x by -30, forearm +20), body pitches forward 15, then the legs fold shut (leg about x by -15, shin +25) as the rear drags up behind. Or just slide it between hops; the hop is what sells it. Attack: the spring. Body pitches forward 30 to 40 degrees and rises, legs straighten (leg +40, shin -50), arms come up and out. Jumpscare: head and stitched mouth into the camera, arms either side. Limits: leg 40, shin 50, arm 45, forearm 40, head 35 any axis. The shoulders are thin; past 45 degrees the arm leaves its socket. The hands are part of the forearm and do not articulate. Parts: sway_1: the tail: a short rope with a tuft, hangs over the rear; sway_2: black strands hanging from under the muzzle; sway_3: black strands hanging from under the muzzle; sway_4: black strands hanging from under the muzzle.

Bent over backwards into a bridge, the yoga wheel: belly to the ceiling, hands and feet flat on the floor. The hands are at the front with the fingers pointing back toward the feet; the feet are behind, toes pointing away. The worm stands straight up out of a hole in the top of the arch, leans back a little, then hooks over so the mouth faces forward at 2.55 m. The head hangs upside down off a snapped neck, under the chest between the hands: crown nearly on the floor, horn pointing down at it, rolled 35 degrees onto one side and turned 17, so the face is upside down and looking at you. A broken end of bone sticks out of the split in the neck. The pelvis is the starved one of the old stage 2, lying on its back, with the emptied plush hanging off it toward the floor. Sides: arm_L, forearm_L, leg_L and shin_L are on +x, the side they are on as it walks (the costume, lying on its back, would call that its right). eye_L and eye_R keep the head's own sides, so with the head upside down eye_L is on -x. The rest pose is the idle: it holds the bridge and trembles, a fast jitter of 1 to 2 degrees on the arms and legs, and the body sinks and lifts 2 to 3 cm as if the arms might give. The head swings loose on the neck (neck 10 degrees, head 15, lagging the body) and never aims at anything. The eyes are what is alive in the head: eye_R, the pinprick, holds on the player (at rest it is already turned up toward a standing player in front, as far as the socket lets it); eye_L, all pupil, aims off to the side and arrives late or not at all. Each carries one catchlight of eye_glow. Eyes: 25 degrees any axis from rest before the iris turns under the socket. The worm is the chain extra_1 (in the wound) to extra_1_12, with the mouth as extra_1_13; each link turns about its joint with the one before. Links 1 to 8 rise out of the belly, 9 to 12 curl over into the hook. A positive turn about x leans the upright links forward and pitches the hook down. Idle: a slow travelling sway, 4 to 8 degrees per link about x and z with a phase lag up the chain, and a swallowing pulse (scale links 1.0 to 1.08 in sequence). The mouth holds on the player while the body under it drifts. extra_2, extra_3, extra_4 are the three tooth rings (outer to inner): spin each about its local z, alternate directions. extra_5 is the second mouth down the throat: slide it out along +z by up to 0.22 m and back. Walk: a scuttling crab walk, head end first. Move the limbs in diagonal pairs (arm_L with leg_R, then arm_R with leg_L), quick, 3 to 4 steps a second, with a dead stop every few steps. The pair in the air swings forward and out: arm about x by -20 to -25, about z by 10 outward (arm_L positive, arm_R negative), forearm by -15 more so the hand lifts; leg about x by -20 and 10 outward about z, shin +15. The pair on the floor sweeps back by as much. The body rolls 4 degrees about z toward the planted pair and bobs 3 cm. To turn, sweep both arms the same way about y by up to 20. The worm lags the body: links 1 to 6 lean back 3 degrees each as it speeds up, while the mouth keeps facing where it is going. Attack: it drops (root down 0.12 m, elbows and knees bending 20 degrees) as the worm rears back (links 7 to 12 by -10 each about x, which lifts the hook and tips the mouth up), then whips forward (links 1 to 6 by +8 each, 7 to 12 by +12) so the mouth comes down to chest height in front of it, while the limbs straighten and the root lunges forward. Jumpscare: straighten the upper links toward the camera so the mouth fills the view, spin the rings fast, push extra_5 out. Under it the upside-down face swings up into the bottom of the frame on the broken neck (neck by -20 about x, head by -25), eye_R on the camera. The inside of the mouth is modelled and textured to hold at close range. Limits: 25 degrees per worm link on any axis before the joints open; link 1 (extra_1) 15, it sits in the wound. Arm 40 any axis, forearm 45, leg 35, shin 40, neck 20, head 35. Parts: extra_2: tooth ring 1 of 3 in the worm mouth (19 hooked teeth, outer). Spin it about its own z; turn neighbouring rings opposite ways; extra_3: tooth ring 2 of 3 in the worm mouth (14 hooked teeth, middle). Spin it about its own z; turn neighbouring rings opposite ways; extra_4: tooth ring 3 of 3 in the worm mouth (10 hooked teeth, inner). Spin it about its own z; turn neighbouring rings opposite ways; extra_5: the second, smaller mouth deep in the throat. Slide it toward +z (out of the mouth, up to 0.22 m) and spin it; sway_1: the tail: a short rope with a tuft, hangs over the rear; sway_10: drool hanging from the lower lip of the worm mouth; sway_2: ropes of dried blood hanging from the underside of the arch, under the wound; sway_3: black strands hanging off the upside-down face toward the floor, some clotted with blood; sway_4: black strands hanging off the upside-down face toward the floor, some clotted with blood; sway_5: black strands hanging off the upside-down face toward the floor, some clotted with blood; sway_6: black strands hanging off the upside-down face toward the floor, some clotted with blood; sway_7: slime strands hanging under worm link 8; sway_8: slime strands hanging under worm link 10; sway_9: slime strands hanging under worm link 12.
